sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·荣森，欢迎收听《重塑者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着你最珍视的 300 件宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重塑者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, the president says things are going to be different in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 今天，总统表示阿富汗的情况将会有所不同。

sentences.en: No more nation building, just killing terrorists.
sentences.zh: 不再进行国家建设，只负责消灭恐怖分子。

sentences.en: But a closer examination suggests this new strategy looks a lot like the strategy of the last 16 years.
sentences.zh: 但仔细审视后会发现，这一新战略看起来与过去 16 年的战略如出一辙。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, August 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是 8 月 23 日，星期三。

sentences.en: Can you remind me when you were in Afghanistan?
sentences.zh: 你能提醒我你是什么时候在阿富汗的吗？

sentences.en: So, I was in Afghanistan in 2002 for a little bit, in and out, and then 2008 to 2014.
sentences.zh: 我在 2002 年去过阿富汗待了一小会儿，进进出出，然后是 2008 年到 2014 年。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, you were basically stationed there.
sentences.zh: 所以你基本上是驻扎在那里。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I covered Afghanistan from 2008 to 2014.
sentences.zh: 我从 2008 年到 2014 年一直在报道阿富汗。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right, right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: In my mind, somehow, you were a Marine, maybe because of the hair, but I remember you were actually just a reporter.
sentences.zh: 在我印象中，你一直是个海军陆战队员，可能是因为你的发型，但我记得你其实只是个记者。

sentences.en: But that's a lot.
sentences.zh: 但这已经很了不起了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I look tough, but I'm not.
sentences.zh: 我看起来很强硬，但我其实不是。

sentences.en: I think you're pretty tough.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你挺强硬的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: We're jumping in.
sentences.zh: 我们切入正题吧。

sentences.en: Matt Rosenberg, what is the theory of nation building in Afghanistan?
sentences.zh: 马特·罗森伯格，阿富汗的国家建设理论是什么？

sentences.en: How and when did this begin?
sentences.zh: 它是如何以及何时开始的？

sentences.en: So, you know, you've got the September 11th attacks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，发生了 9·11 袭击事件。

sentences.en: Today, our fellow citizens, our way of life, our very freedom came under attack in a series of deliberate and deadly terrorist acts.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们的同胞、我们的生活方式、我们珍视的自由，遭到了一系列蓄意且致命的恐怖袭击。

sentences.en: Within a month, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 不到一个月，美国

sentences.en: is in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 就进入了阿富汗。

sentences.en: It's pushing to help kind of oust the Taliban.
sentences.zh: 它在推动帮助推翻塔利班。

sentences.en: America strikes back.
sentences.zh: 美国进行反击。

sentences.en: Afghanistan is pounded with bombs and missiles from the Aran Sea.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗遭到来自阿拉伯海的炸弹和导弹的猛烈轰炸。

sentences.en: That doesn't take very long, but by the middle of 2002, things are, the Taliban's gone and the country's stabilizing.
sentences.zh: 这没花太长时间，但到 2002 年年中，事情进展顺利，塔利班已经消失，国家正在趋于稳定。

sentences.en: The liberation of that country was the beginning of the long and unrelenting struggle we have entered.
sentences.zh: 那个国家的解放，是我们所参与的这场漫长而无情斗争的开始。

sentences.en: But what the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但美国

sentences.en: inherits there is a country that doesn't have a functioning government.
sentences.zh: 在那里接手的是一个没有正常运作政府的国家。

sentences.en: There's nothing to take over.
sentences.zh: 根本没什么可接管的。

sentences.en: So you're either going to leave and the Taliban are going to come back or you're going to build a state.
sentences.zh: 所以你要么离开，让塔利班卷土重来，要么就去建立一个国家。

sentences.en: So very early on, we're nation building.
sentences.zh: 所以很早的时候，我们就在进行国家建设了。

sentences.en: There was no choice.
sentences.zh: 当时别无选择。

sentences.en: My fellow citizens, at this hour, American and coalition forces are in the early stages of military operations to disarm Iraq, to free its people,
sentences.zh: 我的同胞们，此时此刻，美国及其盟军正处于解除伊拉克武装、解放其人民的军事行动初期，

sentences.en: and to defend the world from grave danger.
sentences.zh: 并保护世界免受严重威胁。

sentences.en: Then 2003 rolls around, and the U.S.
sentences.zh: 然后到了 2003 年，美国

sentences.en: invades Iraq.
sentences.zh: 入侵了伊拉克。

sentences.en: It was this short, and this is what happened.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样，发生得很快。

sentences.en: And that immediately sucks up a tremendous amount, both the bandwidth and the military power that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这立刻消耗了美国手中大量的资源，

sentences.en: has on hand.
sentences.zh: 包括带宽和军事力量。

sentences.en: We weren't pouring our best minds and best people into the problem.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有把最优秀的人才和资源投入到这个问题上。

sentences.en: So in 2004, 5, 6, the Taliban, who had retreated to these havens in Pakistan, those who had escaped, they start filtering back in in greater numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以在 2004、2005、2006 年，那些撤退到巴基斯坦避难所的塔利班成员，那些逃脱的人，开始大量潜回。

sentences.en: And they start really sowing the seeds of a renewed insurgency.
sentences.zh: 他们开始真正播下叛乱重燃的种子。

sentences.en: And by 2008, during the presidential campaign, Obama runs partly on...
sentences.zh: 到了 2008 年总统竞选期间，奥巴马竞选纲领的一部分就是……

sentences.en: The central front in the war on terror is not Iraq.
sentences.zh: 反恐战争的中心战线不是伊拉克。

sentences.en: And it never was.
sentences.zh: 从来都不是。

sentences.en: Getting out of Iraq and getting into Afghanistan to not lose it.
sentences.zh: 撤出伊拉克，进入阿富汗，以防输掉那里的战争。

sentences.en: And when he gets into office, you know, he orders up a bunch of assessments and finds out it's worse than he thought.
sentences.zh: 当他上任后，你知道，他下令进行了一系列评估，发现情况比他想象的还要糟糕。

sentences.en: Afghanistan has not loSt.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗并没有输。

sentences.en: But for several years, it has moved backwards.
sentences.zh: 但几年来，它一直在倒退。

sentences.en: And at that point, he then starts sending in more troops.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，他开始增派部队。

sentences.en: And as commander-in-chief, I have determined that it is in our vital national interest to send an additional 30,000 U.S.
sentences.zh: 作为三军统帅，我已决定，增派 3 万名美军

sentences.en: troops to Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 前往阿富汗符合我们的重大利益。

sentences.en: The whole idea was to give the time and space needed to build an Afghan government that can run the country.
sentences.zh: 整个想法是给予必要的时间和空间，建立一个能够治理国家的阿富汗政府。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That can win people over from the Taliban side.
sentences.zh: 一个能够将民众从塔利班阵营争取过来的政府。

sentences.en: And that those two pressures will then bring the Taliban to the table.
sentences.zh: 这两股压力将迫使塔利班坐到谈判桌前。

sentences.en: That's the idea.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个想法。

sentences.en: What actually is nation-building?
sentences.zh: 到底什么是国家建设？

sentences.en: What does that mean on the ground?
sentences.zh: 在实地这意味着什么？

sentences.en: Nation-building is kind of this top-to-bottom exercise where at the very top,
sentences.zh: 国家建设是一种自上而下的实践，在最顶层，

sentences.en: you'd have senior officials working with other senior Afghan officials to help them build government ministries.
sentences.zh: 你会看到高级官员与阿富汗高级官员合作，帮助他们建立政府部门。

sentences.en: But then you get down to the village level where, you know, a lot of Afghan villages never had any government to begin with.
sentences.zh: 但当你深入到村庄层面时，你知道，许多阿富汗村庄最初根本没有任何政府。

sentences.en: I mean, this is one of the poorest countries in the world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是世界上最贫穷的国家之一。

sentences.en: And you'd get there.
sentences.zh: 当你到达那里时，

sentences.en: I remember going on these embeds.
sentences.zh: 我记得我曾随军采访。

sentences.en: You'd be with some company commanders, 27-year-old guy.
sentences.zh: 你会和一些连长在一起，那是个 27 岁的年轻人。

sentences.en: He would have to get to know all the elders in the area.
sentences.zh: 他必须去结识该地区所有的长老。

sentences.en: And they would have what they call shuras, kind of like this quasi-town hall-type meeting-type thing to talk about some problem.
sentences.zh: 他们会举行所谓的“舒拉”（shuras），类似于一种准市政厅式的会议，来讨论某些问题。

sentences.en: Did they need an irrigation ditch or can I give you some money for this?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要一条灌溉渠，还是我可以给你们一些钱来解决这个问题？

sentences.en: And you quickly get into these kind of absurdist places where, you know, they want to have a shura for the elders of the village.
sentences.zh: 你很快就会陷入这种荒诞的境地，你知道，他们想为村里的长老开个会。

sentences.en: They buy a bunch of goats.
sentences.zh: 他们买了一堆山羊。

sentences.en: And you're asking how much they paid for the goats.
sentences.zh: 你问他们买了多少钱。

sentences.en: They're paying two or three grand a goat.
sentences.zh: 他们一只羊付了两三千美元。

sentences.en: And you're like, the golden price of a goat here is about $100.
sentences.zh: 而你会觉得，这里山羊的正常价格大约是 100 美元。

sentences.en: So, I mean, that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: So, nation-building is really complicated because if you're pumping in money into a place with very little structure,
sentences.zh: 所以，国家建设真的很复杂，因为如果你把钱投入到一个结构非常薄弱的地方，

sentences.en: you're going to end up in a pretty quickly situation with a lot of corruption, a lot of inefficiencies, and just a lot of real challenges.
sentences.zh: 你很快就会陷入腐败丛生、效率低下以及各种现实挑战的境地。

sentences.en: Can you explain to me in simple terms where we're at in the war in Afghanistan right now?
sentences.zh: 你能用简单的语言向我解释一下我们目前在阿富汗战争中的处境吗？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Since the end of 2014, Afghan forces have been doing the fighting, most of the fighting.
sentences.zh: 自 2014 年底以来，阿富汗军队一直在进行战斗，大部分的战斗。

sentences.en: At the end of 2014, the Americans and their European partners went into what they call a purely trained, advised, and assist role where they're supposed to help the Afghans fight.
sentences.zh: 2014 年底，美国及其欧洲伙伴转入所谓的纯粹训练、建议和协助角色，他们本应帮助阿富汗人作战。

sentences.en: This is under President Obama, sort of saying like it's your war now.
sentences.zh: 这是在奥巴马总统任期下，相当于说“现在是你们的战争了”。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We do a little medevac, a little bit of air support, but we're pretty under-resourced, as the military would say.
sentences.zh: 我们做一点医疗后送，一点空中支援，但用军方的说法，我们资源相当不足。

sentences.en: And there's a smaller counterterrorism mission of mostly special ops guys and CIA guys who go out and like kill al-Qaeda and ISIS.
sentences.zh: 还有一个规模较小的反恐任务，主要是特种部队和中情局人员，他们负责出去消灭基地组织和伊斯兰国。

sentences.en: Since then, the Afghans have been losing.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，阿富汗人一直在输。

sentences.en: There's no other way around it.
sentences.zh: 这是无法回避的事实。

sentences.en: The Taliban steadily gaining territory.
sentences.zh: 塔利班在稳步夺取领土。

sentences.en: At one point in 2015, they took over a whole city for a few days before the Americans helped beat them back.
sentences.zh: 2015 年有一次，他们占领了整个城市几天，直到美国人帮助将其击退。

sentences.en: And I think where we really are is something that every military strategist, political strategist here has to wrestle with, which is a simple problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们现在的处境是每一位军事战略家、政治战略家都必须面对的问题，这是一个简单的问题。

sentences.en: We're putting in more troops right now and more resources so we can provide more air support, training, medical evacuation to Afghan forces.
sentences.zh: 我们现在投入更多的部队和资源，以便为阿富汗军队提供更多的空中支援、训练和医疗后送。

sentences.en: The Taliban has none of that, yet they're winning.
sentences.zh: 塔利班什么都没有，但他们却在获胜。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because they've got momentum on their side and they are not fighting for people who they believe are corrupt.
sentences.zh: 因为他们有势头，而且他们不是在为他们认为腐败的人而战。

sentences.en: They're fighting for people they believe in.
sentences.zh: 他们是在为他们信仰的人而战。

sentences.en: The Afghan soldiers aren't.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗士兵则不然。

sentences.en: Their leadership is divided.
sentences.zh: 他们的领导层分裂了。

sentences.en: Those who aren't corrupt are fighting with each other.
sentences.zh: 那些不腐败的人也在互相争斗。

sentences.en: And look, I mean, the corruption there, it's hard to overstate.
sentences.zh: 听着，我的意思是，那里的腐败程度，很难被夸大。

sentences.en: There was one point where the Americans had all these anti-corruption task forces going.
sentences.zh: 有一次，美国人开展了所有这些反腐败特别工作组的工作。

sentences.en: And this other very senior American rightly observed, how are we going to crack down on corruption?
sentences.zh: 另一位非常高级的美国官员正确地观察到，我们要如何打击腐败？

sentences.en: If we try to arrest every corrupt government minister, a cabinet minister, there'd be one left who wasn't arrested.
sentences.zh: 如果我们试图逮捕每一个腐败的政府部长、内阁部长，最后只会剩下一个没被逮捕的。

sentences.en: Is what you're saying, Matt, that the Taliban is fighting for a war that they believe in?
sentences.zh: 马特，你的意思是塔利班是在为他们信仰的战争而战吗？

sentences.en: And the United States and the Afghan military that we've tried to prop up are not fighting for a war that they believe in as much.
sentences.zh: 而美国和我们试图扶持的阿富汗军队并不是在为他们同样信仰的战争而战？

sentences.en: Is that why you're saying the Taliban is winning?
sentences.zh: 这就是你认为塔利班正在获胜的原因吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they have support of the people.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们得到了民众的支持。

sentences.en: It's hard to measure, but they're clearly some support.
sentences.zh: 这很难衡量，但显然存在一些支持。

sentences.en: They're clearly giving them shelter and it's not entirely all born of fear.
sentences.zh: 他们显然在为他们提供庇护，而且这并不完全源于恐惧。

sentences.en: We are not nation building again.
sentences.zh: 我们不再进行国家建设了。

sentences.en: We are killing terrorists.
sentences.zh: 我们是在消灭恐怖分子。

sentences.en: So President Trump on Monday seemed to set up nation building as this unattractive alternative to just killing terrorists.
sentences.zh: 所以特朗普总统周一似乎将国家建设设定为一种比单纯消灭恐怖分子更缺乏吸引力的选择。

sentences.en: Is that a dichotomy that exists strategically in the world that you inhabit?
sentences.zh: 在你所处的这个世界里，这是一种战略上存在的二分法吗？

sentences.en: You talk to lots of military.
sentences.zh: 你和很多军方人士交谈过。

sentences.en: You know, it's hard to say.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很难说。

sentences.en: I think his allergy to nation building isn't unique all across the political spectrum.
sentences.zh: 我认为他对国家建设的排斥在整个政治光谱中并不罕见。

sentences.en: There are a lot of people who would make a strong case that no matter what our intentions are, no matter what our resources are, strong countries build themselves.
sentences.zh: 有很多人会提出强有力的论据，认为无论我们的意图如何，无论我们的资源如何，强大的国家都是靠自己建立起来的。

sentences.en: That somebody from the outside isn't going to be able to build a strong country.
sentences.zh: 外人是不可能建立起一个强大的国家的。

sentences.en: And there's, look, there's decades of evidence in parts of the world where we've collectively,
sentences.zh: 而且，你看，在世界某些地区有几十年的证据表明，我们集体，

sentences.en: the global community has spent hundreds of billions of dollars doing development work and hasn't gone in anywhere.
sentences.zh: 全球社会已经花费了数千亿美元进行发展工作，但哪里都没有成功。

sentences.en: But this idea that we can just purely go kill terrorists, that there's some kind of military solution here,
sentences.zh: 但认为我们可以纯粹去消灭恐怖分子，认为这里存在某种军事解决方案，

sentences.en: I don't think you can find a person on the planet who's seriously engaged in Afghanistan and spend time there that believes there is a pure military solution here.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你在地球上能找到一个认真参与阿富汗事务并在那里待过的人，会相信这里存在纯粹的军事解决方案。

sentences.en: This is not a war of annihilation like World War II where we're going to crush Germany and Japan.
sentences.zh: 这不是像二战那样我们要摧毁德国和日本的歼灭战。

sentences.en: You know, there's nobody there to crush.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那里没有人可以摧毁。

sentences.en: The crushing the Taliban would be crushing a great many Afghans.
sentences.zh: 摧毁塔利班就等于摧毁了许多阿富汗人。

sentences.en: If you're trying to keep this from becoming a haven for militants and others, then just killing them doesn't actually accomplish that.
sentences.zh: 如果你想防止这里成为武装分子和其他人的避风港，那么仅仅消灭他们并不能真正实现这一目标。

sentences.en: Then you need to create a real country that's strong enough to enforce its laws, to control its own borders, and to give its people a reason not to give haven to these groups.
sentences.zh: 那么你需要创造一个真正的国家，它足够强大，能够执行法律，控制自己的边界，并给人民一个不为这些组织提供庇护的理由。

sentences.en: Well, so let's talk about what seemed like a kind of new idea for a minute.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们来谈谈那个看起来像是一种新想法的事情。

sentences.en: And that was President Trump as a candidate.
sentences.zh: 那就是作为候选人的特朗普总统。

sentences.en: He campaigned on the idea that this strategy in Afghanistan would be to not be in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 他竞选时提出的想法是，阿富汗战略应该是“不在阿富汗”。

sentences.en: So that was different.
sentences.zh: 所以那是不一样的。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What happens so that Trump says what he said on Monday night?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么导致特朗普说了周一晚上那样的话？

sentences.en: Ladies and gentlemen, the President of the United States.
sentences.zh: 女士们，先生们，美利坚合众国总统。

sentences.en: Look, you can't discount the role of politics here.
sentences.zh: 听着，你不能忽视政治在这里的作用。

sentences.en: You certainly don't want to be the president who lost Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 你当然不想成为那个输掉阿富汗战争的总统。

sentences.en: And that was certainly most likely going to be the case if you just pull troops out immediately.
sentences.zh: 如果你只是立即撤军，那几乎肯定会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: Also, don't discount the presence of a number of generals in his administration who all played significant roles in the Afghan war and pushed him towards this.
sentences.zh: 此外，不要忽视他政府中许多将军的存在，他们都在阿富汗战争中发挥了重要作用，并推动他走向这一步。

sentences.en: General McMaster is actually a great example here.
sentences.zh: 麦克马斯特将军就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: He was in Afghanistan in 2010 and 11.
sentences.zh: 他曾在 2010 年和 2011 年在阿富汗。

sentences.en: He ran this big anti-corruption task force.
sentences.zh: 他负责过这个大型反腐败特别工作组。

sentences.en: I think in both Afghanistan and in Iraq, we didn't pay enough attention to the political dynamic.
sentences.zh: 我认为在阿富汗和伊拉克，我们都没有足够重视政治动态。

sentences.en: For example, in Afghanistan, and we're trying to overcome all of this now in Afghanistan, but in Afghanistan,
sentences.zh: 例如在阿富汗，我们现在正试图克服所有这些问题，但在阿富汗，

sentences.en: if you think about the way the military was going around telling everyone who would listen that the greatest single threat to Afghanistan was what he called criminal patronage networks.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想军方当时到处告诉每一个愿意倾听的人，说阿富汗面临的最大单一威胁是他所谓的“犯罪庇护网络”。

sentences.en: That is, a bunch of senior officials all out to enrich themselves and help each other out.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，一群高级官员一心只想中饱私囊，互相勾结。

sentences.en: Actually, many of these criminal networks became stakeholders in state weakness because it's the weakness of these institutions that gave them impunity, freedom of action,
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多这样的犯罪网络成了国家软弱的利益相关者，因为正是这些机构的软弱给了他们豁免权、行动自由，

sentences.en: and so forth.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: He said that and the Taliban havens in Pakistan, those were the big issues.
sentences.zh: 他说，再加上塔利班在巴基斯坦的避难所，这些才是大问题。

sentences.en: If you didn't solve that, you couldn't win the war.
sentences.zh: 如果你不解决这些，你就无法赢得战争。

sentences.en: So it sounds like these generals made peace with what they think is necessary and, I guess, what the president was willing to agree to.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来这些将军们已经与他们认为必要的事情达成了妥协，我想，也与总统愿意同意的事情达成了妥协。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what was our strategy in Afghanistan before Monday night?
sentences.zh: 那么周一晚上之前，我们在阿富汗的战略是什么？

sentences.en: It was this train to advise and assist the strategy.
sentences.zh: 就是这种训练、建议和协助的战略。

sentences.en: The thing is, I'm not sure that's entirely changed right now because, you know, looking at what President Trump said, he spoke in incredibly vague terMs.
sentences.zh: 问题是，我不确定现在情况是否完全改变了，因为你看，看看特朗普总统所说的，他用的词非常模糊。

sentences.en: A lot of we're going to win, a lot of, you know, victory as a clear definition, a lot of rhetoric, but not a lot of clear ideas there.
sentences.zh: 很多“我们要赢”，很多关于“胜利”的清晰定义，很多空话，但并没有多少清晰的思路。

sentences.en: And his top advisors were offering a totally different view, saying the ultimate solution was, you know, going to be peace talks with the Taliban,
sentences.zh: 而他的高级顾问们提出了完全不同的观点，说最终的解决方案是与塔利班进行和平谈判，

sentences.en: that they would submit to negotiations because we would show more military force now because Trump was in charge.
sentences.zh: 因为特朗普掌权，我们会展示更多的军事力量，所以他们会屈服于谈判。

sentences.en: The thing is, that's not a new idea.
sentences.zh: 问题是，这并不是什么新主意。

sentences.en: That was the whole idea behind the surge.
sentences.zh: 这正是当年“增兵”背后的全部想法。

sentences.en: When President Obama ordered it up was, you know, we get the military in there, they beat back the Taliban, the Taliban, cry uncle, we got to have peace talks.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统下令增兵时，我们的想法是，我们把军队派进去，打退塔利班，塔利班就会求饶，我们就能进行和平谈判。

sentences.en: We had 100,000 troops then, you know, and 40,000 European troops there as well.
sentences.zh: 那时我们有10万军队，还有4万欧洲军队在那里。

sentences.en: We're now down to 13,000 when all this is said and done, plus a few thousand Europeans.
sentences.zh: 现在一切尘埃落定，我们只剩下1.3万人，外加几千名欧洲人。

sentences.en: So why is this going to work now when it didn't work then?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么当时行不通的事情，现在却能行得通呢？

sentences.en: It sounds like what you're saying, Matt, is that every president has had some schizophrenic kind of debate within it, the Bush administration, the Obama administration,
sentences.zh: 马特，听起来你的意思是，每一任总统内部都存在某种精神分裂式的辩论，布什政府、奥巴马政府，

sentences.en: now maybe even the Trump administration, around the question of am I nation building or am I just killing the enemy?
sentences.zh: 现在甚至可能是特朗普政府，都在纠结于“我是在进行国家建设，还是仅仅在消灭敌人”这个问题。

sentences.en: That this is the back and forth that every president has already experienced.
sentences.zh: 这就是每一任总统都已经经历过的反复拉锯。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think if the military has the same problem, they really have two minds.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果军方也有同样的问题，他们确实是心口不一。

sentences.en: We've got to go out and fight.
sentences.zh: 我们必须出去战斗。

sentences.en: We've got to do this.
sentences.zh: 我们必须这样做。

sentences.en: But, oh, no, this is a political problem.
sentences.zh: 但是，哦，不，这是一个政治问题。

sentences.en: We can't shoot our way out of it.
sentences.zh: 我们无法通过武力解决它。

sentences.en: So far, we haven't found any way out of it.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，我们还没有找到任何解决办法。

sentences.en: But there have just been moments.
sentences.zh: 但确实有过一些时刻。

sentences.en: I'm looking at these Rex Tillerson, the Secretary of State, just at a press conference.
sentences.zh: 我正在看国务卿雷克斯·蒂勒森刚才的新闻发布会。

sentences.en: And there are things, I'm looking at the transcript right now.
sentences.zh: 我手头正看着文字记录，里面有些内容。

sentences.en: It's like we could be in 2005, we could be in 2009, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, statements saying things like.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们就像回到了2005年，或者2009、10、11、12、13、14、15年，声明里说着这样的话：

sentences.en: We chose not to just focus on Afghanistan, but we undertook a fairly comprehensive review of our relationships in Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 我们选择的不仅仅是关注阿富汗，而是对我们与巴基斯坦的关系进行了相当全面的审查。

sentences.en: Talking about Pakistan, you know, the Taliban have a safe haven in Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 谈到巴基斯坦，你知道，塔利班在巴基斯坦有避难所。

sentences.en: We have spent 16 years trying to figure out how to get Pakistan to stop doing that and to behave much more like an ally.
sentences.zh: 我们花了16年时间试图弄清楚如何让巴基斯坦停止这样做，并表现得更像一个盟友。

sentences.en: The Pakistanis say they are.
sentences.zh: 巴基斯坦人说他们正在这样做。

sentences.en: It's the worst kind of marriage one can imagine.
sentences.zh: 这是你能想象到的最糟糕的婚姻。

sentences.en: Literally, Teller's just now saying Pakistan in particular can play an important role here.
sentences.zh: 实际上，蒂勒森刚才就在说，巴基斯坦尤其可以在这里发挥重要作用。

sentences.en: We stand ready to help Pakistan address terrorist organizations inside of their country.
sentences.zh: 我们随时准备帮助巴基斯坦解决其境内的恐怖组织。

sentences.en: But they must, they must adopt a different approach themselves.
sentences.zh: 但他们必须，他们自己必须采取不同的方法。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a statement that could have been made in 2002, was certainly made in 2011, 12, and 13.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种声明在2002年就能说，在2011、12和13年肯定也说过。

sentences.en: And it's just being said again now as if it's, you know, some kind of new thought or, you know, something worth stating.
sentences.zh: 现在又被说了一遍，好像这是什么新想法，或者什么值得一提的事情。

sentences.en: Is what the president is describing, our nationalist president, this killing terrorists but not nation building,
sentences.zh: 总统所描述的，我们这位民族主义总统所说的“消灭恐怖分子而非进行国家建设”，

sentences.en: is that an inherently less interventionist approach, if we're being honest?
sentences.zh: 如果说实话，这是否本质上是一种干预程度较低的方法？

sentences.en: Is that why he's describing it that way, to kind of save face?
sentences.zh: 这就是他这样描述的原因吗，为了挽回面子？

sentences.en: I think he is.
sentences.zh: 我想他是这样。

sentences.en: I think maybe he believes it.
sentences.zh: 我想也许他自己也相信这一点。

sentences.en: But you also look at the other things he said about the Afghan military helping them fight better.
sentences.zh: 但你也要看看他说的关于阿富汗军队帮助他们更好地战斗的其他事情。

sentences.en: America will continue its support for the Afghan government and the Afghan military as they confront the Taliban in the field.
sentences.zh: 美国将继续支持阿富汗政府和阿富汗军队，因为他们正在战场上对抗塔利班。

sentences.en: Helping Afghanistan pay for itself more.
sentences.zh: 帮助阿富汗更多地实现自给自足。

sentences.en: We are going to participate in economic development to help defray the cost of this war to us.
sentences.zh: 我们将参与经济发展，以帮助抵消这场战争对我们的成本。

sentences.en: I mean, that all involves nation building.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一切都涉及国家建设。

sentences.en: So it's not like we're going to stop doing the things that one would call nation building tomorrow because Trump literally laid out a plan that includes a ton of it.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说我们明天就会停止做那些所谓的国家建设的事情，因为特朗普实际上制定了一个包含大量此类内容的计划。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So what is a terrorist killing in the Trump kind of lexicon and strategy that he is laying out?
sentences.zh: 那么在特朗普的词汇和战略中，所谓的“消灭恐怖分子”到底是什么？

sentences.en: Is it drone strikes?
sentences.zh: 是无人机袭击吗？

sentences.en: Is it done from the air so you don't have as many troops on the ground?
sentences.zh: 是从空中进行，这样地面上就不需要那么多部队了吗？

sentences.en: Is it targeted assassinations from American snipers?
sentences.zh: 是美国狙击手的定点清除吗？

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 到底是什么？

sentences.en: You know, it's hard to say.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很难说。

sentences.en: I imagine it's a combination of all those.
sentences.zh: 我想是所有这些的结合。

sentences.en: A lot of night raids, as they call them.
sentences.zh: 很多他们所谓的“夜袭”。

sentences.en: I don't think the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我不认为美国

sentences.en: likes to use the term targeted assassinations, even though it certainly seems to be what we do.
sentences.zh: 喜欢使用“定点清除”这个词，尽管这看起来确实是我们正在做的事情。

sentences.en: But why can't you just do these assassinations?
sentences.zh: 但为什么不能直接进行这些清除行动呢？

sentences.en: Why can't you just kill terrorists?
sentences.zh: 为什么不能直接消灭恐怖分子？

sentences.en: I mean, you can.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以这样做。

sentences.en: You're just going to create more of them eventually.
sentences.zh: 但你最终只会制造出更多的恐怖分子。

sentences.en: Here's the first of all.
sentences.zh: 首先是这样。

sentences.en: Drone strikes aren't that accurate.
sentences.zh: 无人机袭击并不那么精确。

sentences.en: You know, when you unleash violence, other people get caught up in it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你释放暴力时，其他人也会被卷入其中。

sentences.en: And when you keep people's fathers and brothers, the people you've left behind tend to think their fathers and brothers were good people, even if they weren't.
sentences.zh: 当你扣押人们的父亲和兄弟时，那些被留下的人往往会认为他们的父亲和兄弟是好人，即使他们并非如此。

sentences.en: And you're going to create some more along the way.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，你会制造出更多敌人。

sentences.en: I mean, there's just no way around it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是无法避免的。

sentences.en: You can't kill people without having repercussions.
sentences.zh: 你不可能在杀人的同时不产生后果。

sentences.en: And so we're just going to kill more and hope that ends the problem.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只是要杀更多的人，并希望这能结束问题。

sentences.en: I mean, every time you kill, you create the problem anew.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你每杀一次人，就会重新制造出这个问题。

sentences.en: So if all you do is airstrikes aimed at terrorists, you're saying it's just going to make the American terrorism problem in Afghanistan worse.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你所做的只是针对恐怖分子的空袭，你是说这只会让阿富汗的美国恐怖主义问题变得更糟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Let's also, what is that American terrorism problem in Afghanistan?
sentences.zh: 我们也来谈谈，阿富汗的那个“美国恐怖主义问题”到底是什么？

sentences.en: September 11th was launched from Afghanistan by al-Qaeda.
sentences.zh: 9·11事件是由基地组织从阿富汗发起的。

sentences.en: The Afghans were not really part of al-Qaeda at that point.
sentences.zh: 当时阿富汗人并没有真正参与基地组织。

sentences.en: And the Taliban, the Afghan Taliban, which is distinct from a separate Taliban movement that's developed in Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 还有塔利班，阿富汗塔利班，它与巴基斯坦发展起来的另一个塔利班运动是不同的。

sentences.en: But the Afghan Taliban, as far as I know, has never sought to launch an attack outside its area.
sentences.zh: 但据我所知，阿富汗塔利班从未寻求在其区域外发动袭击。

sentences.en: It's never attacked people in Europe.
sentences.zh: 它从未袭击过欧洲的人民。

sentences.en: It's never attacked the United States, as far as I know.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，它从未袭击过美国。

sentences.en: So who are we fighting there?
sentences.zh: 那么我们在那里是在和谁打仗？

sentences.en: You know, there are remnants of al-Qaeda.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那里有基地组织的残余势力。

sentences.en: There's now an Islamic State branch.
sentences.zh: 现在还有一个伊斯兰国分支。

sentences.en: But the day-in, day-out Taliban, do they have any ambitions beyond Afghanistan?
sentences.zh: 但那些日常的塔利班，他们有超出阿富汗的野心吗？

sentences.en: We've seen very little evidence they do.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎没有看到任何证据表明他们有。

sentences.en: What you're raising, Matt, is one of the great original questions of American intervention in Afghanistan,
sentences.zh: 马特，你提出的问题是美国干预阿富汗最初的重大问题之一，

sentences.en: which is what happens when a culture like the United States sees something in a culture and religion like that practiced by the Taliban that they find somehow abhorrent?
sentences.zh: 那就是当像美国这样的文化看到像塔利班所实践的那种文化和宗教时，觉得某种程度上令人厌恶，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Is that sufficient to try to remake another country's political system?
sentences.zh: 这是否足以尝试重塑另一个国家的政治制度？

sentences.en: It's a really good question.
sentences.zh: 这确实是个好问题。

sentences.en: Now, look, there are a lot of Afghans who oppose the Taliban, who are miserable under Taliban rule and don't want to see us go.
sentences.zh: 现在，听着，有很多阿富汗人反对塔利班，他们在塔利班统治下生活得很痛苦，不想看到我们离开。

sentences.en: So I don't want to make this as like we're coming in and imposing our values.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想把这说成是我们进来强加我们的价值观。

sentences.en: There are many Afghans who share our values.
sentences.zh: 有很多阿富汗人认同我们的价值观。

sentences.en: That said, you know, Trump made it very clear that he's got no interest in human rights.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，你知道，特朗普说得很清楚，他对人权毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: Ultimately, it is up to the people of Afghanistan to take ownership of their future, to govern their society, and to achieve an everlasting peace.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，阿富汗人民有责任掌握自己的未来，治理自己的社会，并实现持久的和平。

sentences.en: We are a partner and a friend, but we will not dictate to the Afghan people how to live or how to govern their own complex society.
sentences.zh: 我们是伙伴和朋友，但我们不会对阿富汗人民指手画脚，告诉他们如何生活或如何治理他们复杂的社会。

sentences.en: And so that's not any part of this anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以这不再是其中的一部分了。

sentences.en: That has been a big part of it, women's rights especially, since the beginning.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，这就是其中的重要部分，尤其是妇女权利。

sentences.en: I mean, women, and this is a great thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，妇女，这是一件伟大的事情。

sentences.en: I think, you know, everybody, both the Afghans and Americans who are involved in this should be proud of this.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，每个人，无论是参与其中的阿富汗人还是美国人，都应该为此感到自豪。

sentences.en: There are women today who work in offices and jobs in Afghanistan that was unmanageable 17 years ago.
sentences.zh: 今天在阿富汗，有妇女在办公室和岗位上工作，这在17年前是不可想象的。

sentences.en: You know, they could barely leave their homes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她们当时几乎无法离开家门。

sentences.en: If there's no interest, then why are we fighting?
sentences.zh: 如果没有兴趣，那我们为什么要打仗？

sentences.en: You know, why not just try and cut a deal to the Taliban now?
sentences.zh: 你知道，为什么不试着现在就和塔利班达成协议呢？

sentences.en: Say, hey, you guys come back, do what you want, just don't let Al-Qaeda be here and get rid of Islamic State.
sentences.zh: 说，嘿，你们回来吧，做你们想做的事，只要别让基地组织待在这里，并除掉伊斯兰国就行。

sentences.en: Would it work?
sentences.zh: 这行得通吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Is it a good idea?
sentences.zh: 这是个好主意吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: We all have our thoughts on that.
sentences.zh: 我们对此都有自己的想法。

sentences.en: But if human rights isn't part of this and democracy, then what are we doing there?
sentences.zh: 但如果人权和民主不是其中的一部分，那我们在那里做什么？

sentences.en: So, Matt, finally, you described a frustrating and a complicated, sometimes impossible-seeming situation in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 所以，马特，最后，你描述了阿富汗一个令人沮丧、复杂，有时看起来不可能解决的局面。

sentences.en: And you seem very skeptical about this latest approach from President Trump.
sentences.zh: 而且你似乎对特朗普总统的最新方针非常怀疑。

sentences.en: I imagine if there was a clear solution to this, we'd know about it, and you'd know about it from your years in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 我想如果这有一个明确的解决方案，我们早就知道了，你也会从你在阿富汗的那些年里知道。

sentences.en: So what can you say about what could be done?
sentences.zh: 那么关于可以做些什么，你能说些什么？

sentences.en: You know, I honestly don't know because there are no good solutions here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我真的不知道，因为这里没有好的解决方案。

sentences.en: Every single one of them is going to involve sacrifice and pain, either on our part or the Afghans' part or both.
sentences.zh: 每一个方案都将涉及牺牲和痛苦，要么是我们这边的，要么是阿富汗那边的，或者两者都有。

sentences.en: You know, if we were to withdraw orderly but quickly, would the Afghan government collapse?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们有序但迅速地撤军，阿富汗政府会崩溃吗？

sentences.en: It may well.
sentences.zh: 很有可能。

sentences.en: If it didn't, if it survived, it's going to be stronger for it, you know?
sentences.zh: 如果它没有崩溃，如果它幸存下来，它会因此变得更强大，你知道吗？

sentences.en: If we stay, are we going to stay for 10, 15, 20 years?
sentences.zh: 如果我们留下来，我们要待10年、15年、20年吗？

sentences.en: Because Trump kept us pretty open-ended.
sentences.zh: 因为特朗普让我们保持了相当开放的结局。

sentences.en: And I know that right now what Trump seems to be doing is a very familiar strategy.
sentences.zh: 我知道特朗普现在似乎在做的是一种非常熟悉的策略。

sentences.en: It's kind of derisively referred to by military types as mowing the grass.
sentences.zh: 被军方人士嘲讽地称为“割草”。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: We're cutting the lawn here.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里修剪草坪。

sentences.en: Or, you know, where terrorists bring up, we cut them down, they grow back, we cut them down some more.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，恐怖分子冒头，我们就把他们割掉，他们又长出来，我们再割掉一些。

sentences.en: That's not a compliment to say you're mowing the grass.
sentences.zh: 说你在“割草”并不是什么恭维话。

sentences.en: But that seems to be what they're doing right now and what we're looking at more of at the moment.
sentences.zh: 但这似乎就是他们现在正在做的事情，也是我们目前看到的更多的情况。

sentences.en: I have to say, you sound exasperated yourself in a way that I find kind of striking, like that you are yourself a little fed up with this.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，你自己听起来很恼火，这让我觉得很震惊，好像你自己也对这一切感到厌倦了。

sentences.en: I mean, it is incredibly frustrating to come back to Washington and listen to this debate just go in circles.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，回到华盛顿听着这场辩论原地打转，真是令人无比沮丧。

sentences.en: It's the same debate, dressed up in slightly new different terms and slightly new different parameters.
sentences.zh: 这还是同样的辩论，只是换了稍微新一点的词汇和稍微新一点的参数。

sentences.en: And maybe the numbers have changed, but none of the ideas are fresh or new.
sentences.zh: 也许数字变了，但没有任何想法是新鲜或创新的。

sentences.en: And look, I hope I'm totally wrong about this.
sentences.zh: 听着，我希望我对此完全错了。

sentences.en: I hope there's something here that I'm not seeing and that we're not seeing.
sentences.zh: 我希望这里有什么我没看到、我们没看到的东西。

sentences.en: It's just given the last 16 years and how much this looks similar in some ways, it's just hard to see how it works.
sentences.zh: 只是考虑到过去16年，以及这在某些方面看起来有多么相似，真的很难看出它怎么能行得通。

sentences.en: Thank you, Matt.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，马特。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激。

sentences.en: All right, man.
sentences.zh: 好的，伙计。

sentences.en: Thanks a lot.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: After the president's speech, a spokesman for the Taliban called it, quote, nothing new.
sentences.zh: 总统演讲后，塔利班的一位发言人称其为“毫无新意”。

sentences.en: And Afghans on the government side had a similar take.
sentences.zh: 政府方面的阿富汗人也有类似的看法。

sentences.en: A member of the Afghan High Peace Council told The Times, that's the same strategy going on the last two decades.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗高级和平委员会的一名成员告诉《泰晤士报》，这与过去二十年里采取的策略如出一辙。

sentences.en: Trump, he added, said we're going to win, but he didn't make it clear how we're going to win.
sentences.zh: 他补充说，特朗普表示我们要赢，但他并没有明确说明我们要如何获胜。

sentences.en: Back in the United States, Breitbart News, with Steve Bannon newly back at the helm, agreed with the Afghans.
sentences.zh: 在美国国内，史蒂夫·班农重掌大权的布赖特巴特新闻网也认同阿富汗人的观点。

sentences.en: It slammed the president for a flip-flop and compared him to President Obama.
sentences.zh: 该网站抨击总统出尔反尔，并将他与奥巴马总统相提并论。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Jorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-乔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zoran Mamdani, and many others, live on stage at The DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 佐兰·马姆达尼以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews at nytimes.com and in the Times app on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com网站和《纽约时报》应用程序上直播部分采访内容。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家届时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你们一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是今天你需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: I'm Admiral Scott Swift, the commander of U.S.
sentences.zh: 我是美国太平洋舰队司令斯科特·斯威夫特海军上将。

sentences.en: Pacific Fleet.
sentences.zh: 太平洋舰队。

sentences.en: I've got a brief statement to make, and I'll take your questions following that statement.
sentences.zh: 我有一个简短的声明要发表，声明结束后我会回答你们的问题。

sentences.en: Divers from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国海军的潜水员

sentences.en: Navy have found the remains of some of the missing sailors aboard the destroyer
sentences.zh: 已经在驱逐舰上发现了部分失踪水兵的遗体，

sentences.en: John S.
sentences.zh: 约翰·S·

sentences.en: McCain, which collided with an oil tanker off the coast of Singapore on Monday.
sentences.zh: 麦凯恩号驱逐舰周一在新加坡海岸附近与一艘油轮相撞。

sentences.en: Ten sailors have been missing since the collision.
sentences.zh: 自碰撞发生以来，已有十名水兵失踪。

sentences.en: Our thoughts and prayers continue to be with the families of those sailors and the families of our sailors who were injured.
sentences.zh: 我们的思念和祈祷将继续与这些水兵的家属以及我们受伤水兵的家属同在。

sentences.en: It's the second time in recent months that a cargo vessel has struck an American Navy ship.
sentences.zh: 这是近几个月来货船第二次撞击美国海军舰艇。

sentences.en: So until we have exhausted any potential of recovering survivors or bodies, the search and rescue efforts will continue.
sentences.zh: 因此，在穷尽所有搜救幸存者或遗体的可能性之前，搜救工作将继续进行。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbar.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Dana.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫达娜。

sentences.en: I am a subscriber to The New York Times, but my husband isn't.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的订阅用户，但我丈夫不是。

sentences.en: And it would be really nice to be able to share a recipe or an article or compete with him in Wordle or Connections.
sentences.zh: 如果能和他分享食谱或文章，或者在Wordle或Connections游戏中一较高下，那该多好啊。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Dana, we heard you.
sentences.zh: 达娜，我们听到了你的心声。

sentences.en: It's why we created The New York Times Family Subscription.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们推出《纽约时报》家庭订阅服务的原因。

sentences.en: One subscription, up to four separate logins for anyone in your life.
sentences.zh: 一份订阅，最多可供你生活中的四个人分别登录使用。

sentences.en: Find out more at nytimes.com slash family.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请访问nytimes.com斜杠family。
